name: Tennessee
tagline: From the Mississippi bluffs at Memphis to Newfound Gap, by way of plateau valleys and TVA lakes.
intro: Tennessee's byways follow the Mississippi along its western edge, run the length of Land Between the Lakes and the Tennessee River, cross the Cumberland Plateau on old pioneer roads and climb into the Smokies and the Cherokee National Forest. This chapter follows the thirteen Tennessee Scenic Byways promoted by the Highway Beautification Office of the Tennessee Department of Transportation, ten of them nationally designated. Unusually, TDOT does not designate byways itself; each one rests on a state Scenic Highway (enacted by the General Assembly) or Tennessee Parkway (named by the Commissioner) designation, and those two longer lists of protected roads are not listed here.

members.name: Great River Road
members.blurb: In Tennessee the river road runs down the Mississippi side of the state, from the bald cypresses of Reelfoot Lake along the Chickasaw Bluffs and the woods of Fort Pillow, a Civil War battle site, to Memphis and Beale Street.

members.name: Woodlands Trace
members.blurb: The Tennessee end of the Trace runs south through Land Between the Lakes to Dover, past bison on the South Bison Range, the old buildings of the Homeplace farm and the ruined Great Western Iron Furnace.

members.name: Natchez Trace Parkway
members.blurb: From Pasquo, south of Nashville, the parkway runs a hundred miles to the Alabama line, crossing Birdsong Hollow on the Double Arch Bridge and passing the grave of Meriwether Lewis, who died on the old Trace in 1809.

members.name: Sequatchie Valley National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: TN 28 and US 127 follow the long Sequatchie Valley from Jasper up through Dunlap and Pikeville, with Walden's Ridge on one side and the Cumberland Plateau escarpment on the other, past the 1851 Bledsoe County jail.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Norris Freeway National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 441 from Rocky Top to Halls, built by the TVA in 1934 to supply Norris Dam, its structures in a matching Art Moderne style. It crosses the dam and follows the Clinch River through the town of Norris.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Cumberland National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Cumberland Gap the byway runs down Powell Valley farmland under the plateau wall, climbs past the Big South Fork, then crosses the tableland past Victorian Rugby and Alvin York's gristmill to Celina, where the Obey meets the Cumberland.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: East Tennessee Crossing
members.blurb: US 25E drops from Cumberland Gap over Clinch Mountain into the Great Valley, through Bean Station, once a Wilderness Road trading post, and Morristown, where Crockett Tavern recalls Davy Crockett's boyhood, then follows US 25 to the North Carolina line.

members.name: Newfound Gap Road
members.blurb: US 441 crosses the Smokies from Gatlinburg to Cherokee on 1930s stone bridges and walls, climbing into spruce-fir forest at Newfound Gap on the state line, where the Rockefeller Memorial stands and a side road climbs to Kuwohi.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Cherohala Skyway
members.blurb: TN 165 climbs out of Tellico Plains through the Cherokee National Forest, from about 900 feet at the Tellico River to more than 5,400 feet near the North Carolina line, on a road local wagon trains campaigned for from 1958.

members.name: Ocoee Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 64 winds past Parksville Lake and up the rocky Ocoee River Gorge, where whitewater events of the 1996 Olympics were held, while Forest Road 77 climbs seven miles to the Chilhowee overlooks.

members.name: Tennessee River Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 440-mile loop of two-lane state roads on both banks of the Tennessee River, joining the river towns of Savannah and Paris with the Civil War ground at Fort Donelson and Shiloh and the TVA story at Johnsonville.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Great Smoky Mountains Byway
members.blurb: US 321 runs some 200 miles along the foothills of the Smokies, from I-75 at Lenoir City through Maryville and Gatlinburg, then on through Newport and Greeneville to Elizabethton near Watauga Lake.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Walton Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 70 follows the 1801 wagon road William Walton cut across the Cumberland Plateau, from Carthage through Cookeville and Crossville, past the falls at Ozone, to the rebuilt Fort Southwest Point above the Clinch at Kingston.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).
